concerns.text: T051 permits reducing permutation shuffles from 10,000 to 1,000 if the 6-hour runtime limit is breached. FR-016 and FR-006 explicitly mandate 10,000 shuffles to achieve a specific p-value resolution (0.0001). Allowing a 10x reduction silently weakens the statistical rigor required by the spec, violating the constraint that the permutation test must use 10,000 shuffles. The task must either guarantee the 10,000 shuffles fit within the time budget or fail the success criterion, rather than relaxing the requirement.

T028 suggests applying PCA to reduce transformer embedding dimensions before VIF calculation if the dimension is 'too high'. FR-009 explicitly mandates computing VIF diagnostics on 'all predictor variables (fingerprint dimensions, 3-D descriptors, and recorded confounders)' and flagging any feature with VIF > 5. Aggregating dimensions via PCA obscures the specific collinearity of individual features, violating the requirement to diagnose all predictor variables individually.

Phase 6 tasks (T060-T064) introduce features (conformational ensembles, H-bond energy potential, rule enumeration) based on 'simulated' reviewer comments (Kandel, Pauling, etc.) that are not present in the Functional Requirements (FR-001 to FR-019) or the Spec. This constitutes unapproved scope creep that adds capabilities not authorized by the spec, violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or expand the spec's demands without explicit authorization.

T013 mandates generating SMILES from 3D geometry if metadata is missing. While the task notes this follows the spec, the Spec (FR-002) states 'Generation uses only bond-connectivity information'. The Plan.md Summary explicitly requires SMILES generation 'strictly from 2D connectivity graphs' to avoid circular dependency. T013's reliance on 3D geometry (even if generated from CIF) risks violating the methodological constraint of using only 2D connectivity for the predictor to ensure independence from the 3D target, creating a potential semantic weakening of the leakage mitigation strategy defined in the Plan.
